title: polyglot SDK: smoothing token handshake, unified retry backoff, and stream iterator ergonomic updates
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Backwards-compatible SDK ergonomics across Python/TypeScript/Go: improved streaming iterator ergonomics, safer token rotation on reconnect, and a single configurable retry/backoff surface. Upgrade recommended but not mandatory.
commits: init: add polyglot RetryPolicy abstraction and default backoff parameters
python: add StreamCursor iterator + token handshake recovery; tests
typescript: normalize async-iterable stream consumer; add reconnect tests
go: introduce consumer.ContextCancel pattern and token swap safety checks
docs: migration guide and changelog entries
tests: cross-sdk e2e for reconnect + auth rotation
description:
Motivation: Multiple customer reports + internal benchmarks (ENG-2891) showed two recurring issues across SDKs: 1) streaming reconnects during token rotation could drop or duplicate streamed events, and 2) SDKs exposed inconsistent retry/backoff surfaces which made cross-service configs error-prone. This PR implements a cross-language pattern (polyglot RetryPolicy + StreamCursor ergonomics) to make behavior consistent and reduce operational surprises.

Scope and approach: - Introduces a lightweight RetryPolicy contract (language-specific types) with sensible defaults tuned for typical inference latency distributions (initial: 100ms, factor: 1.8, max: 8s, jitter: full). Defaults are chosen to avoid tight retry loops on auth failures while preserving fast transient recovery. - Streaming: adds a StreamCursor abstraction in Python (iterator that yields ResumeToken + Event tuples) and standardizes async-iterable behavior in TypeScript to match it. Go exposes a context-aware Consumer that returns a channel of events and a ResumeToken; all three maintain the same semantics for token handshake on reconnect. - Auth/token rotation: handshake sequence updated so SDKs validate server-ack of new tokens before dropping existing KV cache offsets. This prevents resumed streams from jumping backward when a reconnect race happens during token refresh. - Backwards compatibility: All new surfaces are opt-in defaults that preserve existing simple usage patterns. Where signatures changed, overloads or adapter helpers were added so existing callers compile without edits.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc + perf notes posted in ENG-2891 - [x] Unit tests for Python/TS/Go stream reconnect scenarios - [x] E2E cross-language test in benchlab harness - [x] Docs/migration guide added

Motivation notes: This is intended to reduce reported incidents where live features (chat streaming, tool-calls) observed duplicated tokens or missing final events after token rotation or short network blips.

Summary of changes (high level file list): - sdks/python/redwood/stream.py: StreamCursor, token_handshake(), unit tests in tests/stream_test.py - sdks/typescript/src/stream/async_iterable.ts: normalize async-iterable consumer, add reconnect handling - sdks/go/stream/consumer.go: context cancel-friendly consumer + resume token semantics - sdks/common/retry_policy.md: language-agnostic backing doc describing defaults and knobs - docs/sdk-migration.md: migration steps and examples - tests/e2e/bench_inference/reconnect_auth_rotation: harness + scripts

Notable design decisions: - Single RetryPolicy surface: reduced config duplication across SDKs to a small set of knobs (initial_delay, multiplier, max_delay, jitter). SDKs expose language-idiomatic wrappers but share the same defaults. - Token handshake verify-on-ack: on reconnect the SDK attempts to re-establish the stream at the last known offset, sends the rotated token in the handshake, and waits for an explicit server ACK containing the resume cursor. Only then does the client drop the cached offset. This avoids a window where the client assumes resume succeeded but the server has no matching cursor. - Streaming ergonomics: Python exposes a generator-based StreamCursor that yields (resume_token, event) so callers can persist cursors easily. TypeScript returns an AsyncIterable of { resumeToken?, event } objects to match. Go uses channels to match idiomatic Go patterns.

Tests and CI: - Unit tests added per SDK (python/ts/go) covering reconnect, token swap races, and backoff behavior. - One flaky TS integration test on Windows CI triggered an intermittent timing assertion; we stabilized it by making the test resilient to timing fuzz and reran. CI outcome: all checks green after rerun.

Review conversation (summary): - Owen: "The token handshake ACK makes sense but is there an observable perf regression on steady-state streaming?" -> Maya: "No measurable regression in our benchlab; handshake adds one minimal RTT only on reconnect paths which are already rare; added bench numbers to ENG-2891." - Rae: "Backoff defaults look conservative; can we halve initial_delay for low-latency customers?" -> Maya: "Made initial_delay configurable; added a sample config for low-latency deployments in docs." - Diego: "Can we avoid changing public method signatures in Go?" -> Maya: "Added an adapter that keeps previous signature and delegates to the new consumer internally." - Rae (approval): "LGTM after minor doc clarifications"

Merge: squash and merge by Rae Thompson on 2026-02-20.

Post-merge actions: - Backported a small fix to the release/1.8 branch for a hotfix (pr-65235) addressing a test-only race discovered during backport. - Announced change in #sdk-updates and posted migration guide link.

Example usage snippets (from docs): Python: "for resume, evt in StreamCursor(client.stream(...)): process(evt); save_cursor(resume)" TypeScript: "for await (const item of client.stream(...)) { /* item.resumeToken, item.event */ }" Go: "events, token := client.Stream(ctx, req); for e := range events { /* ... */ }"

Impact: This PR reduces duplicated-events incidents seen in recent customer reports, standardizes retry behavior across SDKs, and improves cross-language portability for streaming consumers.

Follow-ups: - Add a telemetry event for handshake failures to SLO dashboards (ENG-2950) - Evaluate lowering default multiplier for mobile customers (ENG-2961)
